newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may need to change credit policy - Keidanren.
newsitem.headline: Japan may need to change credit policy - Keidanren.

text.p: Japan's current low interest rate policy may need to be changed a bit in order to make it more balanced with those of other nations, Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of the nation's powerful business lobby Keidanren, told a news conference on Monday.

"I don't want to talk about something that the Bank of Japan decides, but Japan's discount rate is at present extremely low, and we may need to adjust the level a bit from the viewpoint of balancing it with those in other nations," said Toyoda, who is also chairman of the nation's top automaker Toyota Motor Corp.
The Japanese economy is gradually improving as shown in the central bank's recent "tankan" survey of corporate business confidence, although gaps remain between industries, he said.
Toyoda also urged the government to lower corporate taxes in order to prevent a further outflow of business from Japan.
In fact, tax revenues could increase if a tax cut helps boost corporate business activities, he said.
